78301.subject: America is awash in indignation
78301.body:
The Economist’s week ahead

Автор: The Economist


Автор: The Economist

    
    
    Прочитайте цю статтю на LinkedIn, щоб приєднатися до обговорення
Прочитати на LinkedIn
https://www.linkedin.com/comm/pulse/america-awash-indignation-the-economist-hsowe?lipi=urn%3Ali%3Apage%3Aemail_email_series_follow_newsletter_02%3ByeM6l3T0TYqrXfnOXY2GNg%3D%3D&midToken=AQFTjFOONAfT2w&midSig=1rHmrf2XXjMso1&trk=eml-email_series_follow_newsletter_02-null-0-read_more_banner_cta_&trkEmail=eml-email_series_follow_newsletter_02-null-0-read_more_banner_cta_-null-fz96fz~mth6fhee~2f-null-null&eid=fz96fz-mth6fhee-2f
  
Enjoying this newsletter? Get it in your inbox every weekend, as well as our daily round-up of The Economist’s best journalism, by signing up for free here. If you sense that America’s politics has become angrier in recent years you’re not wrong. We report on new data showing that irate expression has jumped, both on social media and on the floor of Congress. Elsewhere, Iceland surprised the European Union, and perhaps itself, by voting “no” in a referendum on whether to reopen negotiations about joining the bloc. We explain why worries about fish trumped anxiety about geopolitics. Brooke Unger, Senior digital editor What to expect in the week ahead: ▸ India’s first-quarter GDP figures were published today. The country’s economy grew by 7.8% year on year, beating forecasts. (Economists expected robust growth of around 7.2%.) The world’s sixth-largest economy is proving resilient, partly because the government has capped prices charged by state-owned refineries, and has subsidised fertiliser. ▸ Tim Cook, Apple’s chief executive for 15 years, hands the reins to John Ternus tomorrow. Mr Ternus has spent half his life at the tech giant; in 2020 he was put in charge of iPhones, Apple’s most important product. His first test comes on September 9th, when the company unveils its latest phones. Apple has not launched a genuinely novel device in years; Mr Ternus, a gizmo guy, may try to end that dry spell. ▸ The immigration ministers of Germany, Austria, Denmark, Greece and the Netherlands meet in Copenhagen on Friday to discuss sending some migrants to Uganda. In June the EU passed legislation allowing countries to set up “return hubs” in far-flung countries. Migrants would be sent there while arrangements are made to repatriate them. A slew of recent measures has reduced irregular migration sharply. Editor’s picks Quantifying anger in American politics Donald Trump’s rhetoric is insulting, combative and angry. Of course, he is hardly the first politician to cultivate outrage. Spiro Agnew, Richard Nixon’s vice-president, delighted in attacking the press. Newt Gingrich, the former speaker of the House, was a master of ginning up resentment. For decades righteous indignation has been the resting state of Bernie Sanders, an independent senator from Vermont. But new research suggests that American politics is angrier than ever.
